To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photosystem II (PS II) reaction center contains 10–12 chlorophylls (Chl) a and 2 cytochrome b559s (b559s).

(i) photosystem II reaction centers isolated from oxygen‐evolving photosystem II membranes with dodecymaltoside bind about 10 chlorophylls and 2 Cyt‐b‐559s, and (ii) reaction centers isolated with Triton X-100 bind about 4 chlorophylls less than reaction centers isolated with dodecylethoside.

the reaction center isolated with dodecymaltoside contains 12 Chl a per reaction center, and that the reaction center purified with Triton X-100 contains only 8 Chl per reaction center, which is consistent with Triton X100 extracting pigments from the polypeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the pigment content of the photosystem is regulated.
the isolation and characterization of the photochemical apparatus of photosystem II, a complex that is essential for the light‐driven water‐splitting reaction of photosynthesis.
the isolation and characterization of the reaction center of PS II.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction center polypetide of photosystem II is a chlorophyll binding pigment protein, and the reaction center polpeptides of photosystem II and the bacterial reaction center have similar pigment binding capacities.
the reaction center polypetides of photosystem II are capable of binding 8 to 12 chlorophyll a molecules, and that the Triton X‐ 100‐solubilized reaction centers are not fully assembled.
the photosystem II chlorophyll content of the reaction center is 8–12 Chl, and that 2 Cytb‐559 per reaction centers is the most likely stoichiometry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction center from photosystem II binds approximately 10 Chl a per reaction center and 2 Cyt‐b559 per reaction center.
the reaction center polypetides from photosystem II bind approximately 2 Chl a per Cyt b‐ 559, a ratio which is consistent with the pigment binding properties found in the bacterial reaction center.
the photosystem II and bacterial reaction centers have different pigment binding properties, but that both have the ability to bind 2 molecules of cytochrome b.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Triton X100 is not the detergent of choice for isolating reaction centers with their full complement of pigments.
the reaction center polyeptides are the primary pigment‐binding components in photosystem II, not the extrinsic polypeptides.
the photosystem II complex is a very dynamic structure, which can be altered by the choice of detergent.
